title: Add role-templating with KMS usage fencing and lightweight audit veneer
author: Priya Kaur
release_notes: Introduce claim-scoped role templates, KMS usage fencing policy and a lightweight audit veneer that improves provenance stamping for cross-region requests. No customer-facing API changes.
commit_summaries: Introduce role template DSL and compiler
Implement KMS fencing middleware and side-effect metrics
Add audit veneer to stamp KMS provenance and redact high-risk fields
Docs for templates, fencing and veneer
Add CI validation script for role templates
description: Context and motivation: customers and internal platform teams need a way to express reusable, claim-scoped RBAC profiles (for operator/service partitions) while enforcing per-request KMS usage boundaries and improving audit provenance without shipping full-fidelity logs to downstream systems. This PR adds a compact role-templating DSL, enforces KMS 'fencing' at the policy-evaluation layer, and introduces a lightweight audit veneer that stamps and forwards provenance metadata with deterministic redaction rules. Changes: - Role templating DSL and compiler (pkg/rbac/templates.go, pkg/rbac/template_compiler_test.go): small expressive language to generate RBAC bindings by templating on request claims (tenant, data_class, geozone, operator_scope). Templates are validated at CI and at runtime; invalid templates are rejected with clear diagnostics. - KMS usage fencing (pkg/kms/fence/*): middleware that validates that KMS key decisions for a request match the policy-decisions derived from role templates and tenancy claims. On mismatch, request is rejected with 403 and a structured audit entry. Fencing emits metrics (internal/telemetry/metrics_kms_usage.go) for per-tenant KMS hits and fallback events. - Audit veneer (pkg/audit/veneer/*): lightweight forwarder that attaches canonical provenance headers (kms_key_id, residence_assertion, template_id) and applies a configurable redaction policy before forwarding to external sinks. The veneer is intended for cross-zone observability where full logs are not allowed. - Feature gating & rollout (cmd/console/feature_flags.go, pkg/config/feature_gates.go): all behavior gated behind 'rbac-templating' and 'kms-fencing' feature flags; default off for existing customers. - CI & validation (scripts/ci/validate-rbac-templates.sh): lint/validate DSL in CI, unit/integration tests added. - Docs and examples under docs/security/*. Motivation section also lists threat model: accidental cross-region key usage, operator overreach via role proliferation, and audit proof lacking KMS attribution. Migration plan and rollout: feature-gated rollout starting in Canary then Reserved clusters; cross-team migration doc at docs/security/rbac-templating.md. Backwards compatibility: templates compile to existing RBAC bindings; no change to API surfaces. Audit veneer is opt-in per sink. Tests and validation: unit tests for template compiler, integration tests for KMS fencing (including simulated multi-region KMS responses), e2e smoke that validates veneer redaction. CI: initial run had 2 flaky tests; fixed by making the template compiler deterministic in edge-case ordering (see commit 9c3b7a). Security review notes: asked SRE and Security to review the middleware and veneer; added additional defensive checks to avoid leaking tenant identifiers when redaction is enabled. Performance: KMS fencing adds a lightweight policy cache and per-request lookup; benchmark on canary shows median request tail increased by ~2ms with cache warm and 15% throughput reduction in worst-case cold-cache pathological templates. Observability: introduced metrics for KMS decision latencies, fencing rejections, and veneer-forward rates. Review conversation (high-level): - Ethan Martinez: requested stronger error messages for template compilation failures and recommended telemetry tags for operator_scope. Author response: added error codes and appended template_id where available. - Lena Ortiz: requested explicit deny semantics when KMS decisions mismatch (rather than soft-fallback). Author response: implemented strict deny with configurable emergency-fallback mode behind enterprise feature flag. - Kai Nakamura: asked for integration tests that simulate multi-provider KMS failovers. Author response: added integration_test.go and test harness to stub provider responses. - Security review (Margaret Huang): requested proof that veneer redaction rules cover PII edge-cases; added additional unit tests and example redaction configs. CI history: initial run: lint/pass, unit tests/fail(2 flaky), integration/pending. Rerun: all checks pass. Files changed and impact: 18 files, primarily small/new modules and docs. No database schema migrations aside from an index migration to support template lookup (pkg/migrations/20260215_rbac_template_index.sql). Rollout steps included: enable flags in Canary, monitor metrics for fencing rejections and KMS error surface, if >0.5% rejection for production-critical routes roll back. Merge decision: after reviewer sign-offs, security sign-off and green CI, PR merged via squash on 2026-02-18. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-2031 (add more conservative default redaction sets) and SUP-7123 (customer support request to migrate tenant templates). Additional notes: - This PR intentionally keeps the audit veneer separate from heavy audit-shipper code so teams can adopt provenance stamping in regulated regions without changing retention. - Administrators can opt-in to 'emergency-fallback' to automatically route to a backup KMS provider when fencing rejects requests; this is off by default and gated under an enterprise flag. - Documented operator templates example in examples/ops/role-templates.example.yaml. If issues arise after rollout, revert path is to disable 'rbac-templating' feature flag and redeploy the veneer config.
